Hi Kimberley,

The advantage of using continuous-time models/methods is that you don't need to worry about what the best time interval is. You will want to use all of the data.

As for the file formatting issues, when I try to download the attached CSV, I get only three rows of data with mismatch columns? In your errors, fread is also complaining about basic file formatting as well.
Have you tried getting your data onto Movebank? You don't have to make the data public to store it there.

Best,
Chris

On Friday, November 18, 2022 at 6:54:56 AM UTC-5 Kimberley wrote:
Hi,

I'm new to R and the Ctmm package and I'm trying to import my movebank data to R but I seem to keep on getting errors. particularly the error of duplicate items. See the image attached. I tried changing the Id to individual.id and now it takes that column but that did not fix te problem. I think there may be something wrong with how i formulated the timestamp argument. 
I know that the data itself per individual is not overlapping or dublicate.

Also another question, the GPS tracker is solar powered and thus the intervals between the data differs from 10 min to 120 min. What is then the best time interval to use when eg. analysing daily movement and comparing it between individuals.

Thanks in advance,
Kind regards,
Kimberley Schaffer
